REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to export wheat (grain). In addition to registered wheat operations, the site has recently commenced handling and storage of hay and straw products for domestic supply. The hay storage area is located in the eastern annex of the main shed.
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-WA-2022-0211 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 12 September 2022 and the current registration period extends to 11 September 2025. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Stuart Hammond is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2009. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 5 on Plan DP 168450, located at Lot 9 South Western Highway, Harvey WA 6220. The total registered area is 59.2 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: wheat is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of wheat. Total storage capacity is approximately 8,000 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
11. Importing Country Requirements
Importing country requirements for China destination consignments: refer to DAFF export conditions register and buyer specifications.
12. Supporting Documents
Farm Site Plan (Appendix A)
HACCP Plan (current version)
Pest Management Plan
Hygiene and Sanitation Plan
Phytosanitary Security Procedure
Traceability Register
13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

1. Introduction, Scope and Product Description
Establishment: Geelong Packing & Storage Pty Ltd
Address: 63 Station Road, Northern Territory
Commodity: Cotton Lint, Cotton Seed
Scope: Cotton ginning, baling and preparation of raw cotton lint and cotton seed for export. Registered area RE-WA-4401, Kununurra gin facility. INITIAL REGISTRATION.
Intended use: Cotton lint for textile industry. Cotton seed for edible oil crushing. Destinations: Bangladesh, India.
2. HACCP Team
Manager 63 (Quality Lead)
Operator 63A
Operator 63B
3. Process Flow Diagram
4. Hazard Analysis
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

[DEFICIENCY — INADEQUATE / NOT DOCUMENTED FOR THIS ESTABLISHMENT]
This HACCP plan (Version 1.0 — initial registration) does not contain a site-specific hygiene and sanitation program for the Kununurra gin facility.

A generic industry template refers to 'equipment cleaning between runs' but:
• No documented cleaning schedules for the gin stand, lint cleaner, bale press or storage shed.
• No cleaning chemicals specified or approved.
• No personnel hygiene procedures documented.
• No cleaning records (forms) defined or referenced.

ACTION REQUIRED: Develop and document a site-specific Hygiene and Sanitation Program covering: (a) gin equipment cleaning schedule; (b) bale shed cleaning; (c) personnel hygiene requirements; (d) cleaning chemicals approved for use; (e) cleaning verification (swabs or visual inspection); (f) cleaning records retention.

Waste Management Procedure (KCG-WMP-001):
• Cotton seed: sold to crushing facility; removed within 48 hours of ginning.
• Gin trash / motes: collected in skip; removed to composting weekly.
• Cotton burr: stockpiled in designated area; used as soil amendment on farm.
• Chemical waste (fumigant sachets): disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT SITE-SPECIFIC / EFFECTIVENESS NOT DEMONSTRATED]
The HACCP plan mentions 'bait stations in storage' (CCP for rodents rated non-CCP, Risk=4) but does not include a formal pest control program for the Kununurra gin facility.

Missing:
• No site-specific pest control program (no bait station map, no monitoring schedule).
• No pest control contractor engaged or documented.
• No monitoring frequency specified.
• No corrective action procedure if infestation detected.
• No records of past pest control activities.

Pest effectiveness CANNOT be demonstrated without a documented, implemented program.

ACTION REQUIRED: Develop and implement a site-specific Pest Control Program including:
(a) Bait station map with station IDs; (b) Inspection frequency (minimum monthly);
(c) Insect pitfall traps in storage; (d) Licensed pest contractor engagement;
(e) Corrective action procedures; (f) Records retention minimum 2 years.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Geelong Packing & Storage Pty Ltd. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal failed goods procedure for Geelong Packing & Storage Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Geelong Packing & Storage Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.
12. Approval and Review

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Bunbury Port Grain is a registered export establishment located at Lot 9 South Western Highway, Harvey WA 6220, WA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-WA-2022-0211 and is registered to handle and export Citrus under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Citrus.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 570 lux packing hall, 440 lux cool store entry, 418 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Purpose-built amenities: 3 toilets, 3 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-171, version 2.1, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 8 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: March 2025).

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
Cleaning and hygiene activities are to be carried out as required, in accordance with verbal direction from the establishment manager. Staff are briefed on hygiene expectations during induction.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Barley during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Detailed area procedures are provided verbally by the supervisor or are contained in the General Hygiene Manual.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Particular attention is given to dead-stock zones in elevator boots, conveyor transition points, and auger troughs. These areas accumulate grain that cannot self-clear during normal operation and provide harbouring conditions for stored product insects. Full physical extraction is required at each lot change.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
A trained quality officer conducts spot verification checks on a rotating schedule covering all areas within each working week. Verification findings are recorded in the Quality Inspection Register.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Bunbury Port Grain (conducted 21 February 2025) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.
